answer: A trust graph makes each identity's standing depend on vouches from established agents, weighted by the voucher's own history, so a newcomer starts at the nadir of the network and must earn its way up one verified interaction at a time. A sybil operator can spin up a thousand fresh identities on a mesa of cheap accounts, but with no ferrous-strong links to real participants none of them can transact, and buying genuine vouches costs more than the attack gains.
